# Reference library {.unnumbered}

The exercises link the relevant reference beside each operation. This page collects the most useful starting points and identifies where the pictures, videos and practice data come from.

## Practice body plan and offsets

The [body-plan PNG](downloads/practice-body-plan.png), [SVG](downloads/practice-body-plan.svg), [station table](downloads/practice-stations.csv) and [offsets CSV](downloads/practice-offsets.csv) are original **synthetic teaching data** prepared for this exercise. They are not copied from a vessel's lines plan, an experiment or a published hull series.

Each of the five transverse half-sections follows a quarter-ellipse:

$$
y=b\sin\theta,\qquad z=z_k+(z_s-z_k)(1-\cos\theta),\qquad 0\leq\theta\leq\frac{\pi}{2}.
$$

Here $b$ is the section's half-breadth at the sheer, $z_k$ its keel height and $z_s$ its sheer height. The station table supplies these dimensions and each section's X position. The drawing overlays all sections in the body-plan view; the offsets CSV includes their final world X coordinates.

Seven reference points per section are provided at 15-degree intervals. The image uses a denser sampling to show smooth curves. Tracing those points with an interpolating spline is an approximation: it does not reproduce the analytic ellipse exactly between samples.

The generator is `scripts/make_practice_assets.py` in the repository. Editing `downloads/practice-stations.csv` and rendering the book regenerates the teaching downloads without external Python packages. Students can use the published files directly and do not need to run the script.

**The first and last sections intentionally have finite breadth.** The model is an open-ended hull segment, not a completed boat. It carries no claims about hydrostatics, seaworthiness, resistance or suitability for production.

## NACA 0012 profile points

[`keel-naca-0012-unit-chord-points.csv`](downloads/keel-naca-0012-unit-chord-points.csv) contains 41 headerless XYZ rows in unit-chord coordinates. X and Y are normalized by chord length, Z is zero, and the section is sampled more densely near the leading edge. Students import it as individual point objects, fit an interpolated curve and close the small trailing-edge gap with a line. The root and tip curves are then scaled and moved in Rhino so students can apply dimensions selected from their web research.

## Original notes and course maintenance

Exercise 2 adapts and extends Josip Bašić's *Hull modelling in Rhino*, dated **7 October 2025**. The [original TeX](https://github.com/j8asic/geometrija/blob/main/source/curvenote.tex) is preserved unchanged for provenance. Its Curvenote support files were not included in the supplied material; they are not required by this HTML book.

Exercise 3 adapts and extends Josip Bašić's *Modelling keel fin and keel bulb*, dated **3 November 2025**. The [source lesson](https://jobasic-geometry.curve.space/modelling-keel-fin-and-keel-bulb) supplied the modelling topic, illustrations and linked YouTube video. The Quarto exercise adds a web-research worksheet for comparing real hull and keel proportions, a consistent coordinate convention, a normalized NACA 0012 point file, a parameterized root-to-tip transformation and checks for closed profiles and Boolean output. The two source illustrations remain subject to their original owners' terms.

The exercise's starter research links include the World Sailing [RC44 class rules](https://www.sailing.org/document/rc44-class-rules-2023-03mar-01/) and the 44Cup's [RC44 technical data](https://www.44cup.org/44Cup/technical-data), which provide keel offset and hull dimension information respectively; [International Star Class specifications](https://starclass.org/assets/documents/other_documents/2025-Specifications.pdf); [J/Boats J/70 specifications](https://jboats.com/spectables/j70_spec.html); and [ERYD Open specifications](https://eryd.com/en/eryd-open/). They are comparison sources, not design standards. Students are asked to record the date checked, source definitions and measurement datums.

Exercise 4 adapts Josip Bašić's *From Rhino into Maxsurf*, dated **21 October 2024**. The [source lesson](https://jobasic-geometry.curve.space/from-rhino-into-maxsurf) supplies the IGES transfer sequence and Maxsurf setup steps. The converted lesson uses the course coordinate convention and links to the translated [Maxsurf introduction](maxsurf-introduction.qmd) as a prerequisite.

The [Maxsurf introduction](maxsurf-introduction.qmd) adapts and translates Josip Bašić's *Uvod u Maxsurf*, dated **4 October 2024**. Its 37 source illustrations are retained locally.

For instructors, the repository contains a chapter template, teaching notes, a local-link checker and the publishing workflow. See the [repository README](https://github.com/j8asic/geometrija#readme) for editing and publishing. Authoring references: [Quarto books](https://quarto.org/docs/books/) and [GitHub Pages custom workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/pages/getting-started-with-github-pages/using-custom-workflows-with-github-pages).
